title: What is Azure
description: Discover what Microsoft Azure is, how cloud computing works, and the difference between public, private, and hybrid clouds.

data.text: **Microsoft Azure** is a cloud computing platform created by Microsoft. It provides hundreds of services that let you build, deploy, and manage applications through Microsoft's global network of data centers — without having to buy and maintain physical servers yourself.

Cloud computing means using someone else's computers over the internet instead of your own. Instead of buying expensive hardware, you rent computing power, storage, and services from a cloud provider like Azure, and you pay only for what you use.

data.title: Benefits of Cloud Computing
items: **No upfront hardware cost** — pay as you go
**Scale up or down** — add resources when demand is high
**Access anywhere** — use services from any device with an internet connection
**Built-in security** — Microsoft handles patches, firewalls, and compliance

data.text: Not all clouds are the same. There are three main ways to deploy cloud services, and Azure can run in all three.
Cloud services are usually grouped into three categories. Think of them as a pyramid — you manage more as you go down, and Azure manages more as you go up.

data.caption: How much you manage vs. how much Azure manages
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[You manage] --> B[IaaS: Infrastructure as a Service]
    B --> C[PaaS: Platform as a Service]
    C --> D[SaaS: Software as a Service]
    E[Azure manages] --> B
    E --> C
    E --> D
    F[Examples: Azure VMs] --> B
    G[Examples: Azure App Service] --> C
    H[Examples: Microsoft 365] --> D

data.title: Service Models Explained
items: **IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)** — Azure provides the virtual machines, networks, and storage. You manage the operating system, patches, and apps. Think of it like renting an empty apartment: you furnish it yourself.

**PaaS (Platform as a Service)** — Azure provides the servers, runtime, and tools. You just write and deploy your code. Think of it like renting a furnished apartment: everything is ready, you just move in.
**SaaS (Software as a Service)** — Azure (or another provider) hosts a complete application you use directly. Think of it like booking a hotel room: everything is handled for you, you just use it.

terms.definition: Delivering computing services (servers, storage, databases, networking) over the internet.
Infrastructure as a Service — virtualized computing resources over the internet.
Platform as a Service — a development and deployment environment in the cloud.
Software as a Service — fully managed software delivered over the internet.
Cloud services offered by a third-party provider over the public internet.
A mix of public and private cloud services.

data.title: Beginner Tip
data.text: Azure is used by over 95% of Fortune 500 companies. Learning the fundamentals opens doors to many well-paid IT careers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform with hundreds of services
Cloud computing means renting IT resources over the internet
Public clouds serve many customers; private clouds serve one organization
Hybrid clouds mix public and private for flexibility
IaaS gives you infrastructure control; PaaS handles the platform; SaaS is a finished app
data.takeaway: Cloud computing shifts the work of managing hardware to the provider, so you can focus on building solutions.
